subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Triton: Neptune's Captured Moon
description: A quick win: understand Triton: Neptune's Captured Moon.

hook.text: Triton orbits Neptune backward—the only large moon with a retrograde orbit. It was likely captured from the Kuiper Belt.

buildup.text: It's one of the coldest surfaces known: –235°C. Nitrogen ice covers the surface, and geysers blast nitrogen gas upward.

discovery.text: Voyager 2 found active geysers in 1989—dark plumes rising 8 km high, blown sideways by thin winds.

twist.text: Triton's retrograde orbit means tidal forces are slowly shrinking it. In billions of years, it will be torn apart into a ring.

climax.text: Triton may have a subsurface ocean. A proposed Trident mission would search for signs of geological activity and water.

punchline.text: A captured world orbiting backward. Geysers, ice, and a doomed orbit ending in a ring.

quiz.question: Why do scientists believe Triton was captured by Neptune?
options: It orbits in the opposite direction to Neptune's rotation, suggesting it didn't form there
Its chemical composition matches asteroids from the inner solar system
It has no craters, indicating it arrived recently in cosmic terms

details.summary: Triton, Neptune's largest moon, orbits backward (retrograde) — strong evidence that it was captured from the Kuiper Belt. Despite surface temperatures of -235°C, Voyager 2 discovered active nitrogen geysers erupting 8 km high.
details.whyItMatters: Triton is a captured Kuiper Belt object providing a close-up preview of a dwarf planet world. Its active geology at extreme cold temperatures expands our understanding of what drives geological processes in the outer solar system.
takeaways: Captured from the Kuiper Belt, orbits Neptune retrograde
Active nitrogen geysers despite -235°C surface temperatures
Likely harbors a subsurface ocean from tidal heating

faq.question: How was Triton captured?
faq.answer: The leading theory involves a binary Kuiper Belt object encountering Neptune. Gravitational interaction captured one body (Triton) while ejecting the other.

faq.question: Is a mission to Triton planned?
faq.answer: NASA's Trident mission was proposed to fly by Triton but was not selected. The concept of a Neptune-Triton orbiter periodically resurfaces in mission studies. The 2022 Decadal Survey prioritized Uranus first, but a Neptune mission could follow in the 2040s-2050s.
